```{r}
#| include: false
# ---- shared diagram helper for the whole deck -------------------------------
# Running example: SES (PARENTED, BOOKSHOME, TECHHOME) -> Ach = Achievement (READING, MATH, SCIENCE)
# Highlight ids: l1..l6 (loadings), e1..e6 (residuals), g1 (structural path),
#                zA (disturbance), varS (Var of exogenous factor), covSA (factor covariance)
library(ggplot2)

oNG <- "#E07B1A"; BLU <- "#2C6FB5"; MAG <- "#C81E7A"; LIM <- "#6FA80F"
dk <- "#3A3A3A"; GRY <- "#9AA0A6"
ar  <- grid::arrow(length = grid::unit(0.22, "cm"), type = "closed")
ar2 <- grid::arrow(length = grid::unit(0.18, "cm"), ends = "both", type = "closed")

circle <- function(x, y, r = 0.5) {
  t <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 60)
  data.frame(x = x + r * cos(t), y = y + r * sin(t))
}

lvpa_plot <- function(hl = NULL,                       # NULL = colour by parameter type
                      parts = c("meas", "struct"),     # which model parts to draw
                      marker = FALSE,                  # show first loadings fixed to 1
                      factors = c("SES", "Ach"),
                      inds = c("Parent\neducation", "Books\nat home", "Tech\nat home",
                               "Reading", "Math", "Science"),
                      struct_lab = "gamma[1]", dist_lab = "zeta[A]") {
  draw_m <- "meas" %in% parts
  draw_s <- "struct" %in% parts
  # colour / width helpers: type colours by default, magenta-on-grey when highlighting
  col <- function(id, type_col) if (is.null(hl)) type_col else ifelse(id %in% hl, MAG, GRY)
  wd  <- function(id, base) if (is.null(hl)) base else ifelse(id %in% hl, 1.8, 1.0)

  fx <- c(-6, 6); r <- 1.1
  bx <- c(-8.5, -6, -3.5, 3.5, 6, 8.5); by <- -3.4
  fidx <- c(1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2)
  ids_l <- paste0("l", 1:6); ids_e <- paste0("e", 1:6)
  lam <- paste0("lambda[", 1:6, "]")
  eps <- paste0("epsilon[", 1:6, "]")
  lcol <- col(ids_l, BLU); ecol <- col(ids_e, MAG)

  p <- ggplot() +
    geom_polygon(data = circle(fx[1], 0, r), aes(x, y), fill = dk) +
    geom_polygon(data = circle(fx[2], 0, r), aes(x, y), fill = dk) +
    annotate("text", x = fx[1], y = 0, label = factors[1], colour = "white", size = 4.6) +
    annotate("text", x = fx[2], y = 0, label = factors[2], colour = "white", size = 4.6)

  # Var of exogenous factor (self-loop); in meas-only view both factors get one
  loops <- if (draw_s) 1 else 1:2
  for (k in loops) {
    p <- p +
      annotate("curve", x = fx[k] - 0.5, y = 1.0, xend = fx[k] + 0.5, yend = 1.0,
               colour = col("varS", dk), linewidth = wd("varS", 0.9),
               curvature = -1.4, arrow = ar2) +
      annotate("text", x = fx[k], y = 2.25, label = "Var", colour = col("varS", dk),
               size = 4, fontface = "italic")
  }

  if (draw_s) {
    # structural path SES -> Achievement, and the disturbance on Achievement
    p <- p +
      annotate("segment", x = fx[1] + r + 0.1, xend = fx[2] - r - 0.1, y = 0, yend = 0,
               colour = col("g1", oNG), linewidth = wd("g1", 1.3), arrow = ar) +
      annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0.55, label = struct_lab, parse = TRUE,
               colour = col("g1", oNG), size = 6, fontface = "italic") +
      annotate("segment", x = fx[2], xend = fx[2], y = 3.2, yend = r + 0.05,
               colour = col("zA", LIM), linewidth = wd("zA", 0.5), arrow = ar) +
      annotate("text", x = fx[2] + 0.9, y = 3.0, label = dist_lab, parse = TRUE,
               colour = col("zA", LIM), size = 4.6)
  } else {
    # measurement-only view: the factors simply covary
    p <- p +
      annotate("curve", x = fx[1] + 0.9, y = 0.9, xend = fx[2] - 0.9, yend = 0.9,
               colour = col("covSA", dk), linewidth = wd("covSA", 0.9),
               curvature = -0.35, arrow = ar2) +
      annotate("text", x = 0, y = 2.9, label = "Cov", colour = col("covSA", dk),
               size = 4, fontface = "italic")
  }

  if (draw_m) {
    th <- atan2(by + 0.55 - 0, bx - fx[fidx])
    x0 <- fx[fidx] + r * cos(th); y0 <- r * sin(th)
    lab_fix <- if (marker) c("1", lam[2:3], "1", lam[5:6]) else lam
    lw <- wd(ids_l, 1.3); lt <- rep("solid", 6)
    if (marker) lt[c(1, 4)] <- "dashed"
    p <- p +
      annotate("segment", x = x0, xend = bx, y = y0, yend = by + 0.55,
               colour = lcol, linewidth = lw, linetype = lt, arrow = ar) +
      annotate("text", x = 0.5 * x0 + 0.5 * bx + c(-0.55, 0.6, 0.6, -0.6, -0.6, 0.55) * 0.6,
               y = 0.5 * y0 + 0.5 * (by + 0.55) + 0.1,
               label = lab_fix, parse = TRUE, colour = lcol, size = 5, fontface = "italic") +
      annotate("segment", x = bx, xend = bx, y = by - 2.2, yend = by - 0.55,
               colour = ecol, linewidth = wd(ids_e, 0.5), arrow = ar) +
      annotate("text", x = bx, y = by - 2.65, label = eps, parse = TRUE,
               colour = ecol, size = 4)
    for (i in 1:6) {
      p <- p +
        annotate("rect", xmin = bx[i] - 1.1, xmax = bx[i] + 1.1,
                 ymin = by - 0.55, ymax = by + 0.55, fill = dk) +
        annotate("text", x = bx[i], y = by, label = inds[i], colour = "white",
                 size = 3.4, lineheight = 0.9)
    }
  }

  ymin <- if (draw_m) by - 3.2 else -1.8
  ymax <- if (draw_s) 3.6 else 3.3
  p + coord_equal(clip = "off") +
    expand_limits(x = c(-10, 10), y = c(ymin, ymax)) +
    theme_void()
}
```

:::

::: {.column style="width:33%; font-size: 0.8em;"}
**CFA**

To what extent do parent education, books in the home, and technology in the home reflect a single latent socioeconomic status variable?
:::

::: {.column style="width:34%; font-size: 0.8em;"}
**LVPA**

What is the effect of **latent SES** on **latent academic achievement**, when each is measured by several indicators?

```{r}
mv_box <- function(x, label) list(
  annotate("rect", xmin = x - 1.15, xmax = x + 1.15, ymin = -0.55, ymax = 0.55, fill = dk),
  annotate("text", x = x, y = 0, label = label, colour = "white", size = 3.6, lineheight = 0.9)
)
mv_plot <- function() {
  ggplot() +
    annotate("segment", x = 1.25, xend = 2.75, y = 0, yend = 0, colour = oNG, linewidth = 1.3, arrow = ar) +
    annotate("text", x = 2, y = 0.45, label = "a[1]", parse = TRUE, colour = oNG, size = 5, fontface = "italic") +
    annotate("segment", x = 5.25, xend = 6.75, y = 0, yend = 0, colour = oNG, linewidth = 1.3, arrow = ar) +
    annotate("text", x = 6, y = 0.45, label = "b[1]", parse = TRUE, colour = oNG, size = 5, fontface = "italic") +
    annotate("curve", x = -0.55, y = 0.6, xend = 0.55, yend = 0.6,
             colour = dk, linewidth = 0.9, curvature = -1.4, arrow = ar2) +
    annotate("text", x = 0, y = 1.85, label = "Var", colour = dk, size = 4, fontface = "italic") +
    annotate("segment", x = 4, xend = 4, y = 1.85, yend = 0.6, colour = LIM, arrow = ar) +
    annotate("text", x = 4, y = 2.3, label = "zeta[B]", parse = TRUE, colour = LIM, size = 4) +
    annotate("segment", x = 8, xend = 8, y = 1.85, yend = 0.6, colour = LIM, arrow = ar) +
    annotate("text", x = 8, y = 2.3, label = "zeta[R]", parse = TRUE, colour = LIM, size = 4) +
    mv_box(0, "Parent\neducation") + mv_box(4, "Books at\nhome") + mv_box(8, "Reading\nscore") +
    coord_equal(clip = "off") +
    expand_limits(x = c(-1.3, 9.3), y = c(-0.9, 3)) +
    theme_void()
}
mv_plot()
```

## Putting the two parts together  {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.2
lvpa_plot()
```

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
::: {.notes}
Same CFA as the previous slide, but the factor covariance is replaced by a directional path (SES to Achievement), and Achievement gets a disturbance. LVPA = CFA (measurement model) + path analysis among latent variables (structural model). Fundamentally the same: theory motivates every specification decision, and we estimate parameters so the model-implied covariance matrix is as close to the observed one as possible. Key difference: the structural paths connect latent variables, so the regression is (conceptually) free of measurement error in the indicators.

- we are going to spend a lot of time reviewing these parts 1. so they are fresh in our minds, and 2. we will discuss how to work with them together.
:::
:::

# Latent Variable Path Analysis

# Systems of equations

Same recipe as Weeks 3 and 7: build the model as equations first, then map the equations onto a diagram.

## Measurement equations

Each indicator is a function of its latent variable (unchanged from CFA):

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column style="width:50%; font-size: 0.78em;"}
$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{ParentEd} &= \tau_1 + \lambda_1\,\text{SES} + \varepsilon_1 \\
\text{BooksHome} &= \tau_2 + \lambda_2\,\text{SES} + \varepsilon_2 \\
\text{TechHome} &= \tau_3 + \lambda_3\,\text{SES} + \varepsilon_3
\end{aligned}
$$
:::
::: {.column style="width:50%; font-size: 0.78em;"}
$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Reading} &= \tau_4 + \lambda_4\,\text{Ach} + \varepsilon_4 \\
\text{Math} &= \tau_5 + \lambda_5\,\text{Ach} + \varepsilon_5 \\
\text{Science} &= \tau_6 + \lambda_6\,\text{Ach} + \varepsilon_6
\end{aligned}
$$
:::
::::

- Every latent variable gets its **own** set of indicators
- Same symbols as Week 7: τ = intercept, λ = loading, ε = residual

## Structural equations

Latent variables are predicted by other latent variables (same form as Week 3):

$$\text{Ach} = \alpha + \gamma_1\,\text{SES} + \zeta_A$$

- α = intercept, 
- γ₁ = structural path
- ζ<sub>A</sub> = disturbance
- SES is **exogenous**: no equation, just a variance

::: {.fragment}
*Compare:* Books = a₀ + a₁(ParentEd) + ζ<sub>B</sub>. Same form, but the variables are now latent.
:::

## Combined system

Same model, two representations. Matching colors show what maps to what.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column style="width:42%; font-size: 0.62em;"}
**Measurement**
$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{ParentEd} &= \tau_1 + \color{#2C6FB5}{\lambda_1}\,\text{SES} + \color{#C81E7A}{\varepsilon_1} \\
\text{BooksHome} &= \tau_2 + \color{#2C6FB5}{\lambda_2}\,\text{SES} + \color{#C81E7A}{\varepsilon_2} \\
\text{TechHome} &= \tau_3 + \color{#2C6FB5}{\lambda_3}\,\text{SES} + \color{#C81E7A}{\varepsilon_3} \\
\text{Reading} &= \tau_4 + \color{#2C6FB5}{\lambda_4}\,\text{Ach} + \color{#C81E7A}{\varepsilon_4} \\
\text{Math} &= \tau_5 + \color{#2C6FB5}{\lambda_5}\,\text{Ach} + \color{#C81E7A}{\varepsilon_5} \\
\text{Science} &= \tau_6 + \color{#2C6FB5}{\lambda_6}\,\text{Ach} + \color{#C81E7A}{\varepsilon_6}
\end{aligned}
$$

**Structural**
$$\text{Ach} = \alpha + \color{#E07B1A}{\gamma_1}\,\text{SES} + \color{#6FA80F}{\zeta_A}$$
:::

::: {.column width="58%"}

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.2
lvpa_plot()
```

# Systems of equations to path diagrams

## Path diagram review

What do the following represent?

- squares/rectangles
- circles/ovals
- single-headed straight arrow
- curved double-headed arrow

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
::: {.fragment}
- Measured variables
- Latent variables
- A path: a loading (latent → indicator) or a structural path (latent → latent)
- A variance or covariance
:::
:::

## Path diagram: measurement part

If we only had the measurement model, it's a CFA with two correlated factors.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.2
lvpa_plot(parts = "meas")
```

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
::: {.notes}
Key point for later: in a CFA the two factors simply covary. There is no direction.
:::
:::

## Path diagram: structural part

If the latent variables were observed, this is a simple path model (just like Week 3).

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 2.4
lvpa_plot(parts = "struct")
```

- The factor **covariance** is replaced by a **directional** path
- Achievement now gets a **disturbance**; SES keeps a **variance**

::::

## Exogenous vs. endogenous latent variables

*Look at the LVPA diagram.*

1. Which latent variable is exogenous? Which is endogenous?
2. Which variables get a **disturbance**? Which get a **residual**?
3. Which variances are free parameters?

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
::: {.fragment}
1. SES is exogenous. Achievement is endogenous.
2. Disturbance: Achievement only. Residuals: all six indicators.
3. Var(SES), Var(ζ<sub>A</sub>), and six residual variances. Var(Achievement) is **not** a free parameter. It is *implied*: γ₁²·Var(SES) + Var(ζ<sub>A</sub>).
:::
:::

```{r}
#| include: false
sp_ar  <- grid::arrow(length = grid::unit(0.2, "cm"), type = "closed")
sp_ar2 <- grid::arrow(length = grid::unit(0.16, "cm"), ends = "both", type = "closed")

sp_r <- 1.0; sp_hw <- 1.1; sp_hh <- 0.55
sp_pt <- function(nd, tx, ty) {
  dx <- tx - nd$x; dy <- ty - nd$y; d <- sqrt(dx^2 + dy^2); ux <- dx / d; uy <- dy / d
  if (nd$type == "L") return(c(nd$x + sp_r * ux, nd$y + sp_r * uy))
  t <- min(if (ux != 0) sp_hw / abs(ux) else Inf, if (uy != 0) sp_hh / abs(uy) else Inf)
  c(nd$x + t * ux, nd$y + t * uy)
}
sp_circle <- function(x, y, r) {
  t <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 60)
  data.frame(x = x + r * cos(t), y = y + r * sin(t))
}
# nodes: id, type ("L" latent / "M" measured), x, y
# edges: from, to, kind ("load" = measurement, "path" = structural)
# covs:  a, b, curv (curvature of the double-headed arrow)
# dirs:  named list of c(dx, dy) for where a disturbance / loop sits (default up)
shape_plot <- function(nodes, edges, covs = NULL, dirs = list()) {
  rownames(nodes) <- nodes$id
  g <- ggplot()
  segs <- list()
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(edges))) {
    f <- nodes[edges$from[i], ]; t <- nodes[edges$to[i], ]
    p0 <- sp_pt(f, t$x, t$y); p1 <- sp_pt(t, f$x, f$y)
    g <- g + annotate("segment", x = p0[1], y = p0[2], xend = p1[1], yend = p1[2],
                      colour = if (edges$kind[i] == "load") BLU else oNG,
                      linewidth = 1.3, arrow = sp_ar)
  }
  for (id in nodes$id) {
    nd <- nodes[id, ]; inc <- edges[edges$to == id, ]
    if (nrow(inc) > 0) {
      loaded <- any(inc$kind == "load")
      if (loaded) {
        f <- nodes[inc$from[inc$kind == "load"][1], ]
        d <- c(nd$x - f$x, nd$y - f$y); d <- d / sqrt(sum(d^2))
      } else d <- if (is.null(dirs[[id]])) c(0, 1) else dirs[[id]]
      b <- sp_pt(nd, nd$x + 10 * d[1], nd$y + 10 * d[2])
      g <- g + annotate("segment", x = b[1] + 1.5 * d[1], y = b[2] + 1.5 * d[2],
                        xend = b[1] + 0.05 * d[1], yend = b[2] + 0.05 * d[2],
                        colour = if (loaded) MAG else LIM, arrow = sp_ar)
    } else {
      s <- if (!is.null(dirs[[id]]) && dirs[[id]][2] < 0) -1 else 1
      top <- if (nd$type == "L") sp_r else sp_hh
      g <- g + annotate("curve", x = nd$x - 0.5, y = nd$y + s * (top - 0.05),
                        xend = nd$x + 0.5, yend = nd$y + s * (top - 0.05),
                        colour = dk, linewidth = 0.9, curvature = -1.4 * s, arrow = sp_ar2)
    }
  }
  if (!is.null(covs)) for (i in seq_len(nrow(covs))) {
    a <- nodes[covs$a[i], ]; b <- nodes[covs$b[i], ]
    p0 <- sp_pt(a, b$x + 3, b$y); p1 <- sp_pt(b, a$x + 3, a$y)
    g <- g + annotate("curve", x = p0[1], y = p0[2], xend = p1[1], yend = p1[2],
                      colour = dk, linewidth = 0.9, curvature = covs$curv[i], arrow = sp_ar2)
  }
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(nodes))) {
    nd <- nodes[i, ]
    g <- g + if (nd$type == "L")
      geom_polygon(data = sp_circle(nd$x, nd$y, sp_r), aes(x, y), fill = dk)
    else annotate("rect", xmin = nd$x - sp_hw, xmax = nd$x + sp_hw,
                  ymin = nd$y - sp_hh, ymax = nd$y + sp_hh, fill = dk)
  }
  g + coord_equal(clip = "off") +
    expand_limits(x = range(nodes$x) + c(-2.5, 2.5), y = range(nodes$y) + c(-2.5, 3)) +
    theme_void()
}
sp_inds <- function(prefix, lat, cx, cy, offs, dy, side = "below", n = 3) {
  # indicators of latent `lat`, placed relative to the latent
  ids <- paste0(prefix, seq_len(n))
  if (side == "below")
    list(nodes = data.frame(id = ids, type = "M", x = cx + offs, y = cy + dy),
         edges = data.frame(from = lat, to = ids, kind = "load"))
  else
    list(nodes = data.frame(id = ids, type = "M", x = cx + dy, y = cy + offs),
         edges = data.frame(from = lat, to = ids, kind = "load"))
}

mk <- function(id, type, x, y) data.frame(id = id, type = type, x = x, y = y)
off3 <- c(-2.8, 0, 2.8)
```

## Model shapes: three latent variables

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4
i1 <- sp_inds("a", "L1", -9, 0, off3, -3.4)
i2 <- sp_inds("b", "L2", 0, 0, off3, -3.4)
i3 <- sp_inds("c", "L3", 9, 0, off3, -3.4)
shape_plot(
  rbind(mk("L1", "L", -9, 0), mk("L2", "L", 0, 0), mk("L3", "L", 9, 0),
        i1$nodes, i2$nodes, i3$nodes),
  rbind(data.frame(from = c("L1", "L2"), to = c("L2", "L3"), kind = "path"),
        i1$edges, i2$edges, i3$edges))
```

## Model shapes: measured exogenous predictor

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
j <- sp_inds("a", "L", 2, 0, off3, -3.4)
shape_plot(
  rbind(mk("X", "M", -6, 0), mk("L", "L", 2, 0), j$nodes),
  rbind(data.frame(from = "X", to = "L", kind = "path"), j$edges))
```

```{r}
#| echo: false

j <- sp_inds("a", "L", 2, 0, off3, -3.4)
shape_plot(
  rbind(mk("X1", "M", -12, 0), mk("X2", "M", -5, 0), mk("L", "L", 2, 0), j$nodes),
  rbind(data.frame(from = c("X1", "X2"), to = c("X2", "L"), kind = "path"), j$edges))
```

## Model shapes: a more complex model

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.8
k1 <- sp_inds("a", "L1", -8, 3, c(-1.2, 1.2), -6, side = "left", n = 2)
k2 <- sp_inds("b", "L2", -8, -3, c(-1.2, 1.2), -6, side = "left", n = 2)
k3 <- sp_inds("c", "L3", -1, 0, c(-1.4, 1.4), -3.4, n = 2)
k4 <- sp_inds("d", "L4", 6, 0, c(-1.4, 1.4), -3.4, n = 2)
shape_plot(
  rbind(mk("L1", "L", -8, 3), mk("L2", "L", -8, -3), mk("L3", "L", -1, 0),
        mk("L4", "L", 6, 0), mk("X", "M", 10, 3.8), mk("Y", "M", 13.5, 0),
        k1$nodes, k2$nodes, k3$nodes, k4$nodes),
  rbind(data.frame(from = c("L1", "L2", "L3", "X", "L4"),
                   to = c("L3", "L3", "L4", "L4", "Y"), kind = "path"),
        k1$edges, k2$edges, k3$edges, k4$edges),
  covs = data.frame(a = "L1", b = "L2", curv = 0.6),
  dirs = list(L2 = c(0, -1)))
```

## Disturbances vs. residuals {.smaller}

| | Residual (ε) | Disturbance (ζ) |
|:--|:--------------|:----------------|
| Sits on | an **indicator** (measured variable) | an **endogenous latent variable** |
| Part of | measurement model | structural model |
| Represents | random measurement error & variance unique to the indicator | Variance in the latent variable not predicted by predictors |

## Why it matters: LVPA

**Where is the random error in this model?**

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.2
lvpa_plot()
```

::: {.fragment}
**Why it matters:** in MVPA, measurement error sat inside the disturbance. In LVPA, it is separated into ε, so the structural path γ₁ is not diluted by measurement error in the indicators.
:::


# Model-implied covariance matrix

- We only observe the **indicators**, so the model-implied covariance matrix remains among the indicators (here 6 × 6)
- We still use the same path tracing rules to identify it

## Review: path tracing rules

Revisit the rules from [Lecture 3](https://srdevore.github.io/edep_625_sem/lectures/w03_mvpa_specification.html) and [Lecture 7](https://srdevore.github.io/edep_625_sem/lectures/w07_cfa_specification.html).

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column style="width:50%; font-size: 0.8em;"}
**Finding routes**

1. Go backward against an arrowhead, then forward. Never forward-then-backward.
2. Never pass through the same variable twice.
3. At most one curved arrow, only at the turning point.
:::
::: {.column style="width:50%; font-size: 0.8em;"}
**Computing the covariance**

1. Find every valid route.
2. Multiply all coefficients along each route.
3. Multiply by the variance of the route's ultimate common source.
4. Sum across routes.
:::
::::

```{r}
#| include: false
# ---- step-by-step model-implied covariance matrix (lower triangle, 6 x 6) ----
cm_lab <- c("PE", "BH", "TH", "Read", "Math", "Sci")
cm_col <- c(A = "#2C6FB5", B = "#6FA80F", C = "#E07B1A")
sub_n  <- c("₁", "₂", "₃", "₄", "₅", "₆")
cm_type <- function(r, c) if (r <= 3 && c <= 3) "A" else if (r > 3 && c > 3) "B" else "C"
cm_txt <- function(r, c) {
  switch(cm_type(r, c),
    A = if (r == c) paste0("λ", sub_n[r], "²Var(S)\n+Var(ε", sub_n[r], ")")
        else paste0("λ", sub_n[r], "λ", sub_n[c], "\nVar(S)"),
    B = if (r == c) paste0("λ", sub_n[r], "²Var(A)\n+Var(ε", sub_n[r], ")")
        else paste0("λ", sub_n[r], "λ", sub_n[c], "\nVar(A)"),
    C = paste0("λ", sub_n[r], "γλ", sub_n[c], "\nVar(S)"))
}
cm_steps <- list(
  list(c(1, 1)),                                               # 1 Var(PE)
  list(c(2, 1)),                                               # 2 Cov(PE, BH)
  list(c(2, 2), c(3, 1), c(3, 2), c(3, 3)),                    # 3 rest of SES block
  list(c(4, 1)),                                               # 4 Cov(PE, Math)
  list(c(4, 2), c(4, 3), c(5, 1), c(5, 2), c(5, 3),
       c(6, 1), c(6, 2), c(6, 3)),                             # 5 rest of cross block
  list(c(5, 4)),                                               # 6 Cov(Read, Math)
  list(c(4, 4)),                                               # 7 Var(Read)
  list(c(5, 5), c(6, 4), c(6, 5), c(6, 6))                     # 8 rest of Ach block
)
# i = number of steps drawn; emph = outline/emphasize the newest step
cm_mat <- function(i, emph = TRUE) {
  g <- ggplot()
  for (r in 1:6) for (cc in 1:r) {
    g <- g + annotate("rect", xmin = cc - 0.48, xmax = cc + 0.48,
                      ymin = (7 - r) - 0.48, ymax = (7 - r) + 0.48,
                      fill = "grey95", colour = "grey80")
  }
  for (s in seq_len(i)) {
    now <- emph && s == i
    for (cell in cm_steps[[s]]) {
      r <- cell[1]; cc <- cell[2]
      g <- g +
        annotate("rect", xmin = cc - 0.48, xmax = cc + 0.48,
                 ymin = (7 - r) - 0.48, ymax = (7 - r) + 0.48,
                 fill = cm_col[[cm_type(r, cc)]], alpha = if (now) 0.95 else 0.4,
                 colour = if (now) "black" else NA, linewidth = if (now) 1 else 0) +
        annotate("text", x = cc, y = 7 - r, label = cm_txt(r, cc),
                 colour = if (now) "white" else "grey20", size = 2.1, lineheight = 0.9)
    }
  }
  for (k in 1:6) {
    g <- g + annotate("text", x = k, y = 6.8, label = cm_lab[k], fontface = "bold", size = 3.4) +
      annotate("text", x = 0.2, y = 7 - k, label = cm_lab[k], fontface = "bold", size = 3.4)
  }
  g + coord_equal(clip = "off") + theme_void() +
    expand_limits(x = c(-0.1, 6.5), y = c(0.4, 7.1))
}
```

## Allowed or not allowed?

For each example, the **magenta** path is the route to evaluate. Is it an allowed route? Take a stand first, then we'll reveal the answer.

## Allowed or not allowed?

**Route:** Parent education ← SES → Achievement → Math

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.2
lvpa_plot(c("l1", "varS", "g1", "l5"))
```

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
::: {.fragment}
**Allowed.** Backward against λ₁, then forward along γ₁ and λ₅. Each variable appears once.
:::
:::

## Allowed or not allowed?

**Route:** Parent education ← SES → Achievement ← ζ<sub>A</sub>

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.2
lvpa_plot(c("l1", "g1", "zA"))
```

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
::: {.fragment}
**Not allowed.** The route goes forward into Achievement along γ₁, then backward against the arrow from ζ<sub>A</sub>. Forward-then-backward is never allowed.
:::
:::

## Allowed or not allowed?

**Route:** Reading ← Achievement → Math

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.2
lvpa_plot(c("l4", "l5"))
```

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
::: {.fragment}
**Allowed.** Backward against λ₄, forward along λ₅. Achievement is the common source, so we multiply by Var(Ach).
:::
:::

## Allowed or not allowed?

**Route:** Reading ← Achievement ← SES → Achievement → Math

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.2
lvpa_plot(c("l4", "g1", "l5"))
```

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
::: {.fragment}
**Not allowed.** The route passes through Achievement twice. (The SES contribution is already inside Var(Ach).)
:::
:::

## Allowed or not allowed?

**Route:** Reading ← Achievement → Math ← ε<sub>5</sub>

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.2
lvpa_plot(c("l4", "l5", "e5"))
```

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
::: {.fragment}
**Not allowed.** The route goes forward into Math, then backward against the arrow from ε₅. Residuals only show up in the *variance* of their own indicator.
:::
:::


# Implications

## Scale

Every latent variable still needs a scale, **including the endogenous one**.

- Option 1: fix the first loading to 1 (marker indicator)
- Option 2: fix the latent variable's variance to 1

::: {.fragment}
**New twist:** 

Var(Ach) = γ₁²·Var(SES) + Var(ζ<sub>A</sub>) 

- Var(Ach) is *derived*, so we can't fix it directly (it's already set). 
- For endogenous latent variables, use the **marker indicator** (fix the first loading to 1).
:::


::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
::: {.notes}
Exogenous factors can use either option; endogenous factors need the marker (or a more advanced constraint on the disturbance). Simplest default: marker on every factor. Answer to the discussion: a 1-unit change in Achievement is a 1-point change in Reading, the marker indicator.
:::
:::

## Scale: marker indicators in the diagram

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.2
lvpa_plot(marker = TRUE)
```

Dashed paths with a **1** are fixed, so they are not estimated.

## Degrees of freedom

df = information − parameters

Remember from MVPA and CFA, information = p(p + 1) / 2, where **p = the number of measured variables**.

::: {.fragment}
Latent variables add **no** information. Six indicators: 6(7)/2 = **21** pieces of information.
:::

## Parameters (q) to be estimated {.smaller}

| Parameter type | CFA (Week 7) | LVPA |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Loadings (λ) | free ones, after fixing one per factor | same |
| Residual variances of indicators (θ) | one per indicator | same |
| Variance of exogenous latent variable(s) | factor variances (and covariances) | exogenous factors only |
| **Structural paths (γ)** | — | one per arrow between latent variables |
| **Disturbance variances (ζ)** | — | one per endogenous latent variable |

::: {.fragment}
Don't count fixed values (marker loadings, or fixed variances).
:::

## Example: counting parameters

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.2
lvpa_plot(marker = TRUE)
```

::: {.fragment}
Loadings 4 (λ₂, λ₃, λ₅, λ₆) + residual variances 6 + Var(SES) 1 + γ₁ 1 + Var(ζ<sub>A</sub>) 1 = **13**
:::

::: {.fragment}
df = 21 − 13 = **8**
:::

## Practice

Calculate degrees of freedom for the SES → Motivation model (marker indicators on both factors).

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
::: {.fragment}
Same structure as the example: 21 pieces of information, 4 loadings + 6 residual variances + Var(SES) + γ₁ + Var(ζ<sub>M</sub>) = 13. **df = 8.**
:::
:::

## Measurement model first, then structure

*Count parameters for a **CFA** with the same six indicators and two correlated factors. Compare.*

::: {.fragment}
CFA: 4 loadings + 6 residual variances + 2 factor variances + 1 covariance = **13**. df = **8**, the same as the LVPA.
:::

::: {.fragment}
With two latent variables, the structural part is **saturated**: γ₁ and Var(ζ<sub>A</sub>) replace Cov and Var(Ach). So fit tells us only about the **measurement** model.
:::

# Two-step logic:

1. Fit the CFA first. If measurement is poor, no structural interpretation is trustworthy.
2. Replace factor covariances of the CFA with theory-driven structural paths. 

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
::: {.notes}
Discussion prompt: SES → Ach and Ach → SES give identical fit here. Direction comes from theory, not data. Sets up identification and fit next week.
:::
:::

# Specifying LVPA models in Lavaan

## Lavaan syntax review {.smaller}

| Symbol | Name | Diagram element | Example |
|:------:|:-----|:----------------|:--------|
| `=~` | measured by | loading (λ): latent → indicator | `SES =~ PARENTED + BOOKSHOME` |
| `~` | regression | structural path (γ) | `ACH ~ SES` |
| `~~` | covariance | variance, residual variance, disturbance variance | `SES ~~ SES` |
| `*` | fix | marker loading | `SES =~ 1*PARENTED` |
| `:=` | define | new parameter, such as an indirect effect | `ind := a*b` |

: {tbl-colwidths="[8,14,36,42]"}

## Lavaan syntax: measurement + structural {.smaller}

```r
lvpa_model <- '
  # measurement model (first loading fixed to 1 to set the scale)
  SES =~ 1*PARENTED    + BOOKSHOME + TECHHOME
  ACH =~ 1*READING_AVE + MATH_AVE  + SCIENCE_AVE

  # structural model
  ACH ~ SES

  # variance of exogenous latent variable, disturbance of endogenous one
  SES ~~ SES
  ACH ~~ ACH

  # residual variances of indicators
  PARENTED ~~ PARENTED
  BOOKSHOME ~~ BOOKSHOME
  TECHHOME ~~ TECHHOME
  READING_AVE ~~ READING_AVE
  MATH_AVE ~~ MATH_AVE
  SCIENCE_AVE ~~ SCIENCE_AVE
'

fit <- lavaan(lvpa_model, data = dat)
```

- `ACH ~~ ACH` is the **disturbance** variance because ACH is endogenous
- Anything not specified is fixed to 0

## Spot the errors {.smaller}

*This model has three bugs. Find them.*

```r
bad_model <- '
  SES =~ PARENTED    + BOOKSHOME + TECHHOME
  ACH =~ 1*READING_AVE + MATH_AVE + SCIENCE_AVE

  ACH =~ SES

  SES ~~ SES
  # ...residual variances omitted for space
'
```

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
::: {.fragment}
1. SES has no marker (`1*`) and no fixed variance, so its scale isn't set.
2. The structural path should use `~` (`ACH ~ SES`), not `=~` (that says Achievement is *measured by* SES).
3. Missing `ACH ~~ ACH` (the disturbance variance).
:::
:::
